lessons.title: Profit, loss and discount
lessons.programRef: O Level Mathematics — Commercial arithmetic (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Calculate profit, loss and percentage profit or loss.
Calculate selling price after a discount or mark-up.
Find the cost price from a selling price and a percentage.
reviewNotes: Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Profit and loss
blocks.md: Profit = selling price (SP) − cost price (CP) when SP > CP; loss = CP − SP when CP > SP. Percentages are always taken on the **cost price**:

blocks.title: Discount and reverse percentages
blocks.md:
- **Discount**: new price = marked price × (1 − rate); a 15% discount means × 0.85.
- **Reverse**: if SP is 120% of CP, then CP = SP ÷ 1.2. Divide by the multiplier; never subtract the percentage from the SP.
- **Commission** is a percentage of the sales made.

blocks.caption: Cost price and selling price (profit 3 000 FCFA)
blocks.alt: Two bars showing a cost of 25 000 FCFA and a selling price of 28 000 FCFA

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Calculating percentage profit on the selling price instead of the cost price.
- Reverse percentage: 20% profit on CP does not mean CP = SP − 20% of SP.
- A 10% increase followed by a 10% decrease does not return to the start (×1.1 × 0.9 = 0.99).

blocks.title: Example 1: percentage profit
blocks.statement: A trader in Kumba buys a bunch of plantains for 25 000 FCFA and sells it for 28 000 FCFA. Find the percentage profit.

blocks.title: Example 2: reverse percentage
blocks.statement: A shopkeeper sells a radio for 36 000 FCFA, making a profit of 20% on the cost price. Find the cost price.

lessons.title: Simple and compound interest
lessons.programRef: O Level Mathematics — Commercial arithmetic (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Use the simple interest formula I = PRT/100.
Use the compound interest formula for amounts after n years.
reviewNotes: Compound interest with n up to 3 is typical: check the exact limit in the syllabus.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Simple interest
blocks.md: Interest is calculated on the original sum P (the principal) at rate R% per year for T years:
blocks.tex: I = \frac{P R T}{100} \qquad A = P + I

blocks.title: Compound interest
blocks.md: Interest is added to the principal each year, so it earns interest too. After n years the amount is:

blocks.caption: 100 000 FCFA at 10% compound interest
blocks.alt: Bars showing the amount growing from 100 000 to 133 100 FCFA over three years

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Using the compound formula for the interest only: $A$ is the **amount** (principal + interest). Subtract P to get the interest.
- Using months as years: for 6 months T = 0.5.
- Writing R = 0.05 in $\frac{PRT}{100}$: use R = 5.

blocks.title: Example 1: simple interest
blocks.statement: Find the simple interest on 200 000 FCFA for 3 years at 5% per annum.
steps: Use I = PRT/100 with P = 200 000, R = 5, T = 3.

blocks.title: Example 2: compound interest
blocks.statement: A cooperative in Bamenda invests 100 000 FCFA at 10% compound interest per year. Find the amount after 2 years.

lessons.title: VAT, taxes and exchange rates
lessons.programRef: O Level Mathematics — Commercial arithmetic (to be checked)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Convert between FCFA and other currencies given an exchange rate.
Solve problems with bills, rates and wages.
reviewNotes: VAT rate 19.25% (17.5% + 1.75% council surcharge) and the euro peg 655.957 are standard figures but rates can change: check against current law. The 600 FCFA per USD rate is an assumption stated in the exercises.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Value Added Tax (VAT)
blocks.md: VAT is a percentage added to the price of goods and services. In these exercises the rate is taken as **19.25%** (the usual Cameroon rate), so price including VAT = price before VAT × 1.1925. To find the price **before** VAT, divide by 1.1925.

blocks.title: Exchange rates
blocks.md: An exchange rate tells how much of one currency equals one unit of another. The FCFA is fixed to the euro: 1 euro = 655.957 FCFA. Other rates change daily; in exercises the rate is always given.

blocks.caption: Price before VAT plus VAT
blocks.alt: A bar with the price before VAT and a smaller block for the VAT added, giving 95 400 FCFA

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- To remove VAT, divide by 1.1925; do not subtract 19.25% of the VAT-inclusive price.
- Multiplying when you should divide in a currency conversion: always ask whether the answer should be bigger (in FCFA) or smaller.
- Mixing the rate and its inverse (FCFA per dollar, not dollars per FCFA).

blocks.title: Example 1: adding VAT
blocks.statement: A generator costs 80 000 FCFA before VAT. VAT is 19.25%. Find the VAT and the price including VAT.

blocks.title: Example 2: exchange
blocks.statement: Take 1 USD = 600 FCFA (an assumed rate). (a) Convert 120 USD to FCFA. (b) How many dollars can be bought with 90 000 FCFA?
